title: Contextual Information Allocation in Shared-State Cognitive Models: An Information-Theoretic Bound
summary: Context-sensitive behavior can be modeled by enriching an internal state, by allowing a response rule to access context directly, or by preserving a shared state while introducing an auxiliary criterion or control variable. This paper isolates an information-theoretic constraint on the third architecture. Let $C$ denote context, $S$ a candidate internal or latent state, $O$ an observable response, and $M$ an auxiliary variable such that $O\perp C\mid(S,M)$.
